subject: Immunology
vignette: A 34-year-old man is evaluated for a rapidly enlarging cervical mass and night sweats. Biopsy shows a germinal-center-derived B-cell lymphoma, and staging marrow reveals the t(14;18) translocation involving the BCL2 locus. Molecular studies demonstrate marked overexpression of a mitochondrial outer-membrane protein that prevents release of cytochrome c into the cytosol.
question: The protein overexpressed in this patient's tumor most directly inhibits which of the following processes?

options.text: Cytochrome c release and caspase-9 activation by the apoptosome
Fas ligand-mediated cross-linking of the death receptor Fas
Perforin-mediated delivery of granzyme B into the target cell
Assembly of the T cell receptor signaling complex
Class switching of surface IgM to IgG in germinal-center B cells

explanation_correct: The overexpressed protein is BCL2, an anti-apoptotic member of the BCL2 family located on the outer mitochondrial membrane. It binds and sequesters pro-apoptotic effectors such as BAX and BAK, preventing mitochondrial outer-membrane permeabilization, cytochrome c release, and formation of the apoptosome with APAF-1 and procaspase-9. In the intrinsic (mitochondrial) pathway, loss of BCL2 function or a relative excess of BAX/BAK tips the balance toward apoptosis. The t(14;18) translocation places the BCL2 gene under the immunoglobulin heavy-chain enhancer, which is the classic explanation for follicular lymphoma's indolent biology and its relative resistance to chemotherapy-induced apoptosis.

explanation_incorrect.B: Fas-mediated apoptosis proceeds through the extrinsic death-receptor pathway (FADD and procaspase-8) and does not depend on BCL2-regulated mitochondrial permeabilization.
explanation_incorrect.C: Perforin and granzyme B are used by cytotoxic T lymphocytes; BCL2 overexpression in a lymphoma does not block perforin pore formation in the target membrane.
explanation_incorrect.D: T cell receptor assembly is a T cell-specific event involving CD3 chains and the pre-TCR, and has no relationship to the BCL2 protein.
explanation_incorrect.E: Class switching requires activation-induced cytidine deaminase in germinal-center B cells and is a differentiation event, not an apoptotic checkpoint.

educationalObjective: BCL2 blocks the intrinsic apoptosis pathway by preventing cytochrome c release and apoptosome formation; its overexpression via t(14;18) is the hallmark of follicular lymphoma.

subject: Immunology
vignette: A 6-year-old boy is brought for massive, nontender cervical lymphadenopathy, marked splenomegaly, and chronic cytopenias since infancy. Laboratory studies show defective Fas-mediated apoptosis of lymphocytes. He has a known pathogenic mutation in the gene encoding a death receptor on the cell surface. His mother reports that a maternal uncle died in childhood of a similar illness.
question: Which of the following best describes the mechanism by which binding of Fas ligand to this receptor induces apoptosis?

options.text: Activation of APAF-1 and recruitment of procaspase-9
Receptor trimerization with recruitment of FADD and activation of procaspase-8
Release of granzyme B from cytotoxic T cell granules directly into the cytosol
Inhibition of BCL2 by direct physical binding on the mitochondrial membrane
Engagement of the CD3 epsilon chain of the T cell receptor complex

explanation_correct: This child has autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome (ALPS) type Ia, caused by germline mutations in FAS. Fas is a surface death receptor of the TNF receptor superfamily; binding of Fas ligand causes trimerization and clustering of death domains, recruitment of the adaptor FADD, and activation of procaspase-8 within the death-inducing signaling complex. Active caspase-8 then activates downstream effector caspases, and in many cells also cleaves BID to amplify through the mitochondrial pathway. Failure of this extrinsic apoptosis pathway leaves auto-reactive lymphocytes alive, producing lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly, and autoimmune cytopenias; the same outcome is seen in sporadic somatic FAS mutations.

explanation_incorrect.A: APAF-1 and procaspase-9 form the apoptosome of the intrinsic mitochondrial pathway, not the cytosolic death-inducing signaling complex assembled at Fas.
explanation_incorrect.C: Granzyme B is a cytotoxic T cell product delivered through perforin pores and represents the granule-mediated route, not the Fas receptor pathway.
explanation_incorrect.D: BID is cleaved by caspase-8 to amplify mitochondrial apoptosis, but BCL2 is not the receptor that transduces the Fas signal itself.
explanation_incorrect.E: The CD3 epsilon chain belongs to the T cell receptor complex involved in antigen recognition and is unrelated to a death receptor on lymphocytes.

educationalObjective: Fas-Fas ligand signaling kills lymphocytes through the extrinsic pathway (FADD and caspase-8), and defective Fas causes autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome.
